changes: p2: role changed from 'owner' to 'other'. The colophon only says the exemplar was obtained from this person (…karmmācājyayāke kāyāvaḥ, 'having taken it from'). Nothing says the copy belongs to them.

p2: dropped the guṭhi-head ('gosthikā-dhani') explanation. The -yāke ending marks a person ('from …'), and the person carries the title karmācārya, so this is most likely a personal name. The reading of the name itself is still uncertain.
purpose: changed to 'for teaching (his) children'. Newari macā means 'child' and śenayātā means 'in order to teach'. The meaning 'pupils' was dropped.
notes: added that the end title and the Newari note disagree about which text this is, and explained the reading of the purpose phrase.

notes: The Newari note says roughly: 'this Sarasvatī-deva hymn (śirokaḥ = ślokaḥ), taken from [Gvaṃ]stikadhani Karmācārya, was written by Devendra Karmācārya in his own hand (thava āṣalasena) to teach the children (macā … śenayātā)'. 'vava' may be a corruption of 'thava' ('own'), giving 'his own children'. p2 only supplied the exemplar. The name is corrupt: 'gvaṃ stikadhani' could also split as a place or epithet 'Gvaṃ' plus the name 'Stikadhani', or hide some other form. The end title ('śrīskandhapurānya vihnunnārāyaṇāya', i.e. a Viṣṇu/Nārāyaṇa piece from the Skandapurāṇa) does not match the Newari note's 'sarasvati devayā śirokaḥ'. This is probably because the manuscript is a Stotrasaṅgraha and the note covers the whole collection or one hymn in it. The colophon is undated.
